entries.title: Isaiah 60:1
segments:
. ISRAEL'S GLORY AFTER HER AFFLICTION. 
 
    An ode of congratulation to Zion on her restoration at the Lord's second advent to her true position as the mother church from which the Gospel is to be diffused to the whole Gentile world; the first promulgation of the Gospel among the Gentiles, beginning at Jerusalem [

], is an earnest of this. The language is too glorious to apply to anything that as yet has happened. 
 
    1. Arise--from the dust in which thou hast been sitting as a mourning female captive (

). 
 
    shine--or, "be enlightened; for thy light cometh"; impart to others the spiritual light now given thee (
). The Margin and GESENIUS translate, "Be enlightened"; be resplendent with posterity; imperative for the future indicative, "Thou shalt be enlightened" (

). 
 
    glory of the Lord--not merely the Shekinah, or cloud of glory, such as rested above the ark in the old dispensation, but the glory of the Lord in person (

). 
 
    is risen--as the sun (
, Margin).

entries.title: Isaiah 60:2
segments: 2. darkness ... earth--the rest of the earth: in contrast with "light ... upon thee" (
). The earth will be afterwards enlightened through Israel (

). 
 
    be seen--conspicuously: so the Hebrew.

entries.title: Isaiah 60:3
segments:
). 
 
    kings-- (

). 
 
    thy rising--rather, "thy sun-rising," that is, "to the brightness that riseth upon thee."

entries.title: Isaiah 60:4
segments:
4. Lift up ... eyes--Jerusalem is addressed as a female with eyes cast down from grief. 
 
    all they ... they--The Gentile peoples come together to bring back the dispersed Hebrews, restore their city, and worship Jehovah with offerings. 
 
    nursed at thy side--rather "carried at thy side." It is the custom in the East to carry the children astride on the hip, with the arms around the body (

entries.title: Isaiah 60:5
segments:
), namely, the bringing back of thy sons. 
 
    flow together--rather, "overflow with joy" [LOWTH]; or, from a different Hebrew root, "be bright with joy" [GESENIUS] (

). 
 
    fear--rather, beat with the agitation of solemn joy at the marvellous sight [HORSLEY] (

). 
 
    be enlarged--swell with delight. Grief, on the contrary, contracts the heart. 
 
    abundance of ... sea--the wealth of the lands beyond the sea, as in Solomon's time, the type of the coming reign of the Prince of peace. 
 
    converted--rather, "be turned," instead of being turned to purposes of sin and idolatry. 
 
    forces--rather, "riches."

entries.title: Isaiah 60:6
segments: 6. camels--laden with merchandise; the camel is "the ship of the desert" (compare

). 
 
    Midian--east of the Elanitic branch of the Red Sea, and stretching northward along Mount Seir. Associated with the Ishmaelites in traffic (

). 
 
    Ephah--part of Midian, east of the Dead Sea. It abounded in camels (

). 
 
    Sheba--in Arabia-Felix, famed for frankincense and gold (
), which they traded in (

entries.title: Isaiah 60:7
segments: 7. Kedar-- (
), in the south of Arabia-Deserta, or north of Arabia-Petraea; they traded in flocks (

). 
 
    Nebaioth--son of Ishmael, as was Kedar. Father of the Nabatheans in Arabia-Petraea. 
 
    minister--by coming up as an acceptable sacrifice. 
 
    come up with acceptance--that is, acceptably. The rams offering themselves voluntarily (

), without waiting for any other priest, answer to believers strong in faith and lamb-like meekness; and in the white fleece-like robe of sanctity [VITRINGA]. 
 
    house of my glory--the temple (

entries.title: Isaiah 60:8
segments: 8. The prophet, seeing in vision new hosts approaching quickly like a cloud of doves, asks who they are.

entries.title: Isaiah 60:9
segments: 9. (see on

). 
 
    Tarshish first--The ships of Tartessus (see on
, that is, vessels that trade to the most distant regions) will be among the foremost to bring back the scattered Israelites (

). 
 
    their silver--The nations among whom the Jews have been scattered shall help them with their money in returning (
), as was the case at the return from Babylon (
; compare

). 
 
    unto the name ... to the Holy One--rather, because of the name--because of the Holy One (compare
) [LOWTH].

entries.title: Isaiah 60:10
segments: 10. kings ... minister unto thee--(See on

). 
 
    in my wrath I smote thee-- (

entries.title: Isaiah 60:11
segments: ). The gates are ever open to receive new offerings and converts (
). GESENIUS explains it, "may come escorted by a retinue."

entries.title: Isaiah 60:12
segments: 12. For--the reason which will lead Gentile kings and people to submit themselves; fear of the God in Israel (

entries.title: Isaiah 60:13
segments: 13. glory--that is, the trees which adorned Lebanon; emblem of men eminent in natural gifts, devoting all that is in them to the God of Israel (

). 
 
    place of my feet--no longer the ark (
), "the footstool" of Jehovah (
); but "the place of His throne, the place of the soles of His feet, where He will dwell in the midst of the children of Israel for ever," in the new temple (

entries.title: Isaiah 60:14
segments: 14. The sons--Their fathers who "afflicted" Israel having been cut off by divine judgments (

). 
 
    The Zion of the Holy One--The royal court of the Holy One. MAURER translates, "Zion, the sanctuary (holy place) of Israel" (

entries.title: Isaiah 60:15
segments: 15. forsaken-- (

). 
 
    no man went through thee--Thy land was so desolate that no traveller, or caravan, passed through thee; true only of Israel, not true of the Church (

). 
 
    excellency--glory, that is, for ever honored.

entries.title: Isaiah 60:16
segments: 16. suck--Thou shalt draw to thyself and enjoy all that is valuable of the possessions of the Gentiles, &c. (

). 
 
    know--by the favors bestowed on thee, and through thee on the Gentiles.

entries.title: Isaiah 60:17
segments:
17. Poetically, with figurative allusion to the furniture of the temple; all things in that happy age to come shall be changed for the better. 
 
    exactors--namely, of tribute. 
 
    righteousness--All rulers in restored Jerusalem shall not only be peaceable and righteous, but shall be, as it were, "peace" and "righteousness" itself in their administration.

entries.title: Isaiah 60:18
segments: ). Not only shall thy walls keep thee safe from foes, but "Salvation" shall serve as thy walls, converting thy foes into friends, and so ensuring thee perfect safety (

). 
 
    gates--once the scene of "destruction" when victorious foes burst through them (
); henceforth to be not only the scene of praises, but "Praise" itself; the "gates," as the place of public concourse, were the scene of thanksgivings (
). "Judah," the favored tribe, means "praise."

entries.title: Isaiah 60:19
segments: 19. The sun and moon, the brightest objects by day and night, shall be eclipsed by the surpassing glory of God manifesting Himself to thee (

entries.title: Isaiah 60:20
segments: 20. There shall be no national and spiritual obscuration again as formerly (

). 
 
    mourning ... ended-- (

entries.title: Isaiah 60:21
segments: 21. all righteous-- (

). 
 
    inherit ... land-- (

). 
 
    branch of my planting-- (

). 
 
    work of my hands--the converted Israelites (

). 
 
    that I may be glorified--the final end of all God's gracious dealings (

entries.title: Isaiah 60:22
segments: 22. little one--Even one, and that the smallest in number and rank, shall be multiplied a thousandfold in both respects (

). 
 
    his time--not our time; we might wish to hasten it, but it will come in due time, as in the case of Jesus' first coming (
); so in that of the restoration of Israel and the conversion of the world (
